findings.trigger: mypy run: var-annotated on `symbols`; tuple[str] assigned to tuple[()]; generator yields tuple[AST,...] where tuple[Module,...] is expected

findings.remediation: Annotate `symbols: List[PythonSymbol] = []`, `stack: List[Tuple[ast.AST, Tuple[str, ...]]]`, and `scope: Tuple[str, ...]`. Keep the syntax 3.10-compatible (typing.List/Tuple). Do not change behavior.

findings.trigger: BM-2 overhead was 16.23x against a 3.0x bound. Baseline was 2975 PASS/0 fail; this run had 2983 PASS/1 fail. Identity retention was reported false.
findings.impact: Criterion 6 requires evidence-based triage and full identity retention. This is probably a timing flake unrelated to the P2C files, but that is unproven.
findings.remediation: Rerun on a clean base and on the head under the same host. Attach identity diff evidence. Do not relax the threshold.

findings.locator: ccm_python.py tokenize bracket loop (OP tokens only)
findings.trigger: On Python 3.10, f-string replacement fields are a single STRING token. Deep bracket nesting inside f"{((((...))))}" is therefore not counted. On 3.12+ these appear as OP tokens and are counted.
findings.impact: The bracket guard is runtime-dependent. It is bypassable on the best-effort 3.10 host and only fully meaningful on the canonical 3.13.15. Scalar guards are not a sandbox in any case.
findings.remediation: Document in the spec that the bracket guard is canonical-runtime-specific (the spec already says this for tokens). Optionally add a fixed small f-string fixture asserting canonical behavior in the restricted host.

findings.trigger: No fixed test for a lone-CR line ending, a multibyte identifier before a nested def on a later line (byte vs char column), a BOM plus second-line cookie, or a NUL byte (ValueError on 3.10/3.11, SyntaxError on 3.12+).
findings.impact: Unicode byte-mapping and error-mapping regressions could pass the focused suite. These are not current defects.
findings.remediation: Add small frozen literal oracles for these cases, with the digests and offsets computed independently.

coverage: Exact type check uses `type is bytes` before any method call; the Poison subclass is rejected without callbacks.
Order is size, then BOM strip and strict decode, then cookie, then tokenize, then ast.parse, then traversal limits. The decode-before-cookie test exists.
Cookie regex and blank-line regex mirror tokenize's cookie_re/blank_re. First-line precedence and alias rejection were verified by reading and by tests.
Sanitized error is raised outside the except block, so __context__ is None; args are empty and str/repr contain only the code.
Traversal is iterative. Ancestor limit allows 64 enclosing declarations; declaration limit 2048. No partial result is returned.
Byte columns map via physical-line starts plus the BOM offset on line 1; CRLF/CR handling matches the parser's newline translation.
No exec/import/filesystem/network/env access; the side-effect canary is parse-only.
Reprs carry no payload; dataclasses are frozen and slotted.
Restricted three-runtime boundary vectors passed (out-of-band evidence).
gaps: Restricted-vector evidence does not tie librarySha256 to the reviewed file hash; this needs to be verified.
Deep unary/attribute recursion behavior on 3.10 was not reviewed beyond the reliance on the restricted host.
Production adapter and hostile-input admission remain out of scope and held.
